prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (ideology-free, no names)

Core approach
- Five missions: sustained economic growth; clean power by 2030; safer communities with serious violence halved; breaking barriers to opportunity; an NHS fit for the future.
- Initial steps: tight fiscal rules; 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week; new Border Security Command; a public clean-power company; antisocial behaviour crackdown; 6,500 new teachers.

Economy and growth
- Fiscal rules: balance day-to-day budget; debt falling by year five; all major fiscal events independently forecast. No rises to National Insurance, Income Tax rates or VAT. Tackle avoidance (abolish non-dom status; close carried-interest loophole; strengthen HMRC).
- Industrial strategy with a statutory council; sector plans (automotive, life sciences, creative, financial services).
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private investment (ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, green hydrogen).
- Business taxation stability: cap corporation tax at 25% for the parliament; permanent full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- Infrastructure: 10-year strategy; new delivery authority; faster planning for nationally significant projects; nationwide gigabit and 5G by 2030.
- Transport: maintain/renew roads; fix 1m potholes annually; accelerate EV charging and restore 2030 ICE phase-out; bring rail into public ownership as contracts end; empower bus franchising; integrated local transport.
- Housing: 1.5m homes over the parliament; restore mandatory targets; brownfield-first plus strategic “grey belt” release; new towns; more social and affordable homes; mortgage guarantee for first-time buyers.
- Devolution: landmark English devolution law; local growth plans; multi‑year council settlements.
- Migration and skills: reduce net migration via a reformed points-based system linked to domestic training; stronger enforcement on employers.
- Work: “Make Work Pay” package—ban exploitative zero-hours contracts; end fire-and-rehire; day‑one rights; single enforcement body; minimum wage set with cost-of-living remit and no lower adult age bands.
- Small business: tackle late payments; easier exporting; reform British Business Bank and procurement; support Post Office and Horizon justice.

Energy, climate, environment
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, marine; long-duration storage.
- Nuclear: extend existing plants; complete Hinkley Point C; advance Sizewell C and SMRs. Gas kept as strategic reserve.
- North Sea: manage existing fields to end of life; no new oil and gas exploration licences; no coal or fracking.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co‑invest and scale local power projects; Local Power Plan.
- Grid upgrade and market reform; reduce standing charges.
- Warm Homes Plan: £6.6bn to upgrade 5m homes.
- Carbon border adjustment; make UK green finance leader with credible transition plans.
- Water: stronger regulation, automatic fines, bonus bans, independent outlet monitoring.
- Farming and nature: 50% public procurement local/higher standard target; land‑use framework; expand habitats; animal welfare measures (e.g., ban trail hunting, trophy imports, puppy smuggling, snares).

Safety, policing, justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands more officers and PCSOs; national efficiency programme.
- Antisocial behaviour: new Respect Orders; tougher action on shoplifting and assaults on retail workers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions; ban dangerous blades; hold online sellers to account; Young Futures hubs nationwide.
- Violence against women and girls: specialist police units; fast‑track courts; enhanced victim support.
- Police standards: tougher vetting, training, inspectorate powers; child safeguards; expanded fraud strategy.
- Justice: improve charge rates; direct‑entry detectives; victims’ rights strengthened; sentencing review; expand prison capacity; reduce reoffending; probation governance review; action on historical injustices (e.g., duty of candour, inquiry responses).

Opportunity, education, families, housing security
- 3,000 school-based nurseries; free primary breakfast clubs; 6,500 new teachers; strengthen support staff; curriculum and assessment review; SEND inclusion; mental health support in every school.
- Skills: Skills England; devolved adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeships Levy to a flexible Growth and Skills Levy; stabilize higher education and improve access.
- Culture and sport: creative industries plan; stronger ticketing protections; independent football regulator.
- Family security: review Universal Credit; child poverty strategy; abolish Section 21 evictions; renter protections and standards; building safety acceleration; end leasehold for new flats; enable commonhold; tackle “fleecehold”; homelessness strategy; retain state pension triple lock; workplace pension reforms.

Health and care
- NHS: 2m extra annual operations/scans/appointments; shared waiting lists; independent sector capacity; workforce plan reset.
- Double CT/MRI scanners with AI; deliver new hospitals; innovation and clinical trials strategy; upgraded NHS app; maternity safety and maternal mortality gap target; regulate managers; new clinical leadership college.
- Primary care: more GPs; face‑to‑face option; modern booking; continuity incentives; expand pharmacist prescribing; wider direct referrals; pilot neighbourhood health centres.
- Dentistry: 700k urgent appointments; contract reform; supervised tooth brushing for ages 3–5 in high-need areas.
- Social care: National Care Service with national standards; “home first”; Fair Pay Agreement; family visit rights; health–care integration.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke‑free generation; restrict youth‑targeted vaping; limit junk‑food ads to children; under‑16 energy drink sales ban; stronger online safety and gambling reforms; halve healthy life expectancy gap; end new HIV cases by 2030.

Governance and democracy
- Independent Ethics and Integrity Commission; stronger misconduct rules; modernise Commons; restrict second jobs that conflict with duties.
- House of Lords: remove hereditary peers; mandatory retirement at 80; participation and standards; consult on a more representative replacement.
- Elections: improve voter registration; fix ID inconsistencies; votes at 16; stronger donation rules.
- Devolution and intergovernmental reset; Council of the Nations and Regions; updated fiscal frameworks; restore devolved structural-fund decision‑making.

Foreign, security, development, trade
- Strategic Defence Review; path to 2.5% of GDP; unwavering NATO and nuclear deterrent commitments.
- Armed forces support, commissioner, and veteran measures (incl. fee waivers); defence industrial strategy; procurement reform.
- Support for Ukraine, asset use for reconstruction; robust stance on hostile state threats; AUKUS; safeguard Overseas Territories.
- Make Brexit work: better UK‑EU trade in goods and services (e.g., veterinary deal, touring artists, mutual recognition), and a security pact.
- Targeted trade strategy; WTO/CPTPP engagement; sectoral deals; uphold standards.
- Climate leadership abroad: launch a Clean Power Alliance.
- Rebuild development expertise; restore 0.7% GNI for aid when fiscally possible; focus on poverty, instability, women and girls, debt, climate finance.
